claim: A full hands-on undergraduate RF systems course covering VNA measurement, patch antenna design, RF demodulation, and MIMO beam steering can be run for under $9,000 in one-time equipment costs.
stance_target: affordability of hands-on RF/SDR lab curricula for ECE programs
quoted_support: The course can be run for less than $9,000 in one-time costs and is well-received by students as evidenced by survey data, with lab resources available in an open repository.

claim: The open-source LibreVNA offers a wider operating range (100 kHz to 6 GHz) than the popular hobbyist NanoVNA (limited to 1 GHz), making it more suitable for IoT-relevant RF teaching labs.
stance_target: choice of VNA hardware for student RF measurement labs
scope_conditions: comparison of low-cost VNA options for educational RF labs
quoted_support: The LibreVNA is an open-source FGPA-based 2-port vector network analyzer that can characterize RF systems from 100 kHz to 6 GHz. In comparison to the inexpensive NanoVNA popular with hobbyists which is limited to 1 GHz, the LibreVNA offers superior performance with a larger operating frequency range.
numbers: 500 MHz-3 GHz sweep range used in lab

stance_target: curriculum design/sequencing for RF and SDR project-based ECE courses
